title: My first game launches next week, any advice?
author: Tommyruin
selftext:
Hey folks, 

My first game, "[Aita: The Dark Domain](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4730130/?utm_source=x&utm_campaign=showcase_replies&utm_content=reply)" releases on the 1st December, and I'm getting nervous that I'm forgetting something in prep for pressing the big button on Steam (and Google Play, and Apple...) 

For those who have gone through this already, any advice? especially as the game used AI in it's development, should I expect a wave of hate?

It's a pixel-art roguelite card game set in the Etruscan underworld with crossplatform support and solo or online co-op for up to 4!

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Tommyruin could you add more about how AI fit into your development process? Just mentioning that AI was used doesn't cut it. Under Rule 4, promotional posts need to contribute something by discussing how the game was actually made. Otherwise the sub gets buried in ads. If there's no update, this post may be removed.

comments.author: Gustave232
comments.body:
You will get hate for using AI but those people won’t even buy your game so if your game is good it will get the love it deserves regardless of AI usage.  
Good luck!

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body: Thank you! Content creator feedback, andfeedback from my closed beta has been extremely positive, I hope people like it!

replies.author: xXEpic_Dragon_Xx
replies.body: How did u do a closed beta that's the step I'm on but I don't know how to approach it did u have a discord ?

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body:
I was fortunate to be in a number of small gaming communities (from IRL friends to friends made online) who were happy to test (about 20 odd people), to then bringing in content creators to help showcase (and also test) the game. Watching people play is so valuable and I learnt so much from watching people interact with my game.

I spent so long and got so close to it, seeing other people approach it for the first time was so eye opening

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body:
The association helped me find this fun meme

https://i.redd.it/d8nwtvztq64i1.jpeg

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: How long did it take for steam to approve you?

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body: I went through two rounds of approvals over about a month, but I've been approved for release since September!

comments.author: TechnicalCricket774
comments.body: Just curious, development cost wise, ball park how much does creating a game of this caliber cost. It looks really well done, more so then average ai games shown here.

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body:
Thank you! So much time has gone in to it the visual feel of the game, and trying to inject some soul (I even went to a real Etruscan Tomb to check I was doing it right! 😂))

So I've spent probably an average of 20 hours a week on top of a normal 9-5. That would be the biggest expense, but it's just me so I am not counting it so I dont get sad when I don't make it back 😂

So not counting time've been on a $100 plan for about 11 months, and in maybe two of those months I doubled up/overlapped if a new model came out that looked "insane" (normally you have to jump on these things before they dumb them down/FOMO). On top of that, the odd $20 drop on odd assets I've liked or access to specific tools (not all worked, but explorin).

For those subs, it's been supporting other things too, but I'd say 60-70% is on the game dev.

Website hosting, and then the fees to the stores is about $250

So i'd so $1500 give or take a few 100?

https://i.redd.it/lhrtx8dpu64i1.jpeg

comments.author: AlexPriner
comments.body: Balatro inspiration I assume? Looks good, good luck with the launch!

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body:
One of many inspirations yes. Mainly from a clean UI/visual clarity point of view. Balatro is good at putting things where you want to see them, so I learnt from that. 

I originally leaned into it hard, and have since been peeling back the layers to try and distance myself as the gameplay is vastly different/not similar at all! But card games using traditional card style cards will get that association as Balatro was so successful I think

replies.author: AlexPriner
replies.body: It was not a negative association don't get me wrong, but it was the first game I thought about when seeing the video. I can see the work you put into it, and taking inspirations from the best is a good thing.

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body: Thank you so much! Yes I strongly agree. I grew up on Blizzard games, and they very much owned the craft of taking inspiration from things and making them their own. I learned from that too I suppose

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: This looks fun. At this point, it’s less about what settings or options you might not be thinking about with store fronts, or even missing features or missed bugs - it’s all about getting the word out, getting wishlists built up, etc

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body: Thank you so much! Honestly marketing/sharing it has been such a struggle and the hardest part for sure. Getting 1-2 wishlists per day after marketing on 4-5 platforms for over two months is pretty depressing, but I'm at the acceptance stage now and just excited to post the game live!

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body: Is this your first game or have you created games before? And you said AI play tested and balanced the game. Have you personally played the game during the playtest phase and were you able to get human play testers to play and break your game or was breaking the game handled by AI as well? Is the game developed in an engine? I just like asking questions :p

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body:
Hey! 
First game I've created

AI was used for balancing. I basically used it to simulate hundreds of thousands of games to see how my blessings (power ups) were balanced.

I played the game a tonne, hundreds of hours myself plus ~100 hours of external testing. AI never did the game "testing". I found so many things that needed fixing that the AI missed, didn't see etc

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Looks like a good game! Best of luck of to you!

comments.author: GornoUmaethiVrurzu
comments.body: It looks promising but the AI sloppy look definitely shines through a bit. I also don't know what I'm doing looking at your trailer. It's not clear what the actual gameplay is.

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body: Thanks for taking a look! Do you have any specific examples of the AI sloppiness you mention for me to fix after launch?
